items.reader: The document concludes "Can't tell." The test is broken: the test arm changed `snippet_length` as well as the ranker model, so the +0.81% lift on Successful Search Rate can't be credited to the ranker. The test ran to completion (day 14 of 14, about 1,000,000 users per arm, above the planned 900,000). No launch decision should be made from this data. Agree to fix the config so snippet length matches in both arms (or have the owner register it as part of the test) and rerun. Also ask for a pre-exposure comparison and a daily series by days since first exposure, since those two checks didn't run. Don't launch on this result. +0.81% Successful Search Rate (95% interval +0.41% to +1.21%), against a bar of at least +0.50%. The unit is percent change, but the document doesn't say whether it's relative or percentage points: unclear. The lift is confounded. Longer snippets may change clicks and success by themselves, independent of the ranker (the document labels this a guess). The pre-period and novelty checks were not run, so the result is also unverified for baseline drift and novelty effects.
